Our power bills are climbing, and it’s not your imagination. Florida just approved the largest electric rate hike in US history, roughly $7 billion from FPL over four years.

FPL says it’s only about $2.50 more a month for a “typical” home. But that lands on top of bills already up 45% since 2021, and it keeps climbing every year through 2029. In a Miami summer with the AC running non-stop, none of us are “typical.”

Here’s what should make us mad: FPL’s guaranteed profit was set at 10.95%, which the state’s own customer advocate says is the highest utility profit in the lower 48. They found half of every dollar FPL asked for goes to profit and taxes, not the grid. And the office whose job is to represent us, the residential customer, was left out of the final deal, which FPL cut with big businesses instead.

FPL says the money hardens the grid against storms. We decide if that’s worth it.

Cities fought this: Pembroke Pines, Collier, Manatee. I couldn’t find that our own Miami-Dade did the same. And the same FPL is now bidding to build the county’s new trash incinerator. We can’t shop around, we can’t switch. That’s a monopoly. The fight’s now headed to the Florida Supreme Court.

Disclaimer: Commentary based on publicly available records and reporting (FPL, Florida PSC, Office of Public Counsel) as of the posting date. This is not legal or financial advice.
